classes.name: Presidential electors
classes.locator: 3 U.S.C. §§ 1 and 21(1); U.S. Const. art. II, § 1, cl. 2
classes.note: One statewide slate per state (Maine by district from 1972 and Nebraska from 1992 add one per district). Legislatures appointed the electors in some states and years, so those states have no popular vote then.

cadence.locator: 3 U.S.C. § 1 and § 21(1): electors are appointed on election day, the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November every fourth year (uniform day from the Act of January 23, 1845)

appointed.locator: Delaware's legislature chose its electors through 1828 (with South Carolina, the only two states to do so that year)
In 1824 the legislatures of Delaware, Georgia, Louisiana, New York, South Carolina, and Vermont chose the electors; the other eighteen states held a popular vote
South Carolina's legislature chose the state's electors through 1860, the last state to do so
1864: Louisiana's Union legislature named electors without a popular vote, and Congress did not count their votes
1868: Florida's legislature chose the state's electors; no popular vote was held

classes.name: U.S. Senate
classes.locator: U.S. Const. art. I, § 3, cl. 1-2 and amend. XVII
classes.note: Two senators per state in three classes, one class elected every second year for six-year terms; popular election from 1914 under the Seventeenth Amendment.

senate.locator: U.S. Const. art. I, § 3, cl. 2 (senators divided into three classes, one class chosen every second year) and amend. XVII (popular election, ratified April 8, 1913); a state admitted later joins at its first regular election

classes.name: U.S. House of Representatives

classes.note: Every seat every second year; the seats per state follow each decennial apportionment.

cadence.locator: 2 U.S.C. § 7: the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November in every even numbered year; U.S. Const. art. I, § 2, cl. 1: members chosen every second year

classes.name: Tribal executives
classes.note: Chair, president, principal chief, or governor, with the deputy where elected. Rules: (1) load a nation's results only from what its own election body publishes openly; (2) cite that body as the source; (3) never use news tallies, tribal newspapers included, or BIA files in their place, and a nation whose body publishes nothing openly gets a gap row; (4) honor any nation's request to withdraw or limit its data. Each nation's constitution or election code sets its own calendar, recorded with that nation's load.

classes.disposition_reason: Only a partial register: Haas, Ten Years of Tribal Government under I.R.A. (1947), Table A (acceptance votes of the tribes, 1934 to 1936, with dates and yes and no counts) and Table B (constitutions and charters approved to 1947), at thorpe.law.ou.edu/IRA/IRAbook. After 1947 there is no register: each Election Board posts its Certificate of Results locally (25 CFR 81.42), the BIA publishes no central list, and the Federal Register carries only the 2015 procedure rule.
